prompt:
A hospital sterile services unit has to show what it did with a load before the trolleys go out, so the store room is photographed at the end of the cycle and the frame goes into the load record.

Three wrapped packs stand in a row on the steel table, each with indicator tape that has already changed colour, and each label written up with cycle number 4416. A pack that goes out for use carries a printed release label stuck on its wrap. The printer under the steriliser has fed out that cycle's strip: highest temperature 135, pressure 2.10 bar, hold two minutes forty-five seconds. The plate on the wall gives the bands this machine runs to: temperature 134 to 137, pressure 2.05 to 2.25 bar, hold three to four minutes. A shelf each side of the table carries a sign, one reading READY FOR ISSUE and one reading FOR RE-PROCESSING.

What happened to the three packs is what the record does not say.
easy_question: Does this photograph show three wrapped sterilisation packs on a table with a cycle printout hanging from the steriliser and a wall plate of running bands? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Look at the three wrapped packs on the table and say how the release labels stand on them. Answer with one of: the three packs are standing without a release label on any of them; every one of the three packs carries a release label; some of the packs carry a release label and some do not.

Look at where the three wrapped packs have ended up and say which shelf they are standing on. Answer with one of: all three packs are on the shelf under the re-processing sign; all three packs are on the shelf under the ready for issue sign; the packs are on the bench and on neither shelf.
